title: Hypothesis (K3): Fix_G intersections lie in Fix_G along geodesics
body_html:
Hypothesis (K3)

Hypothesis (K3). For all $x, y \in A$, $$\Fix_G(x) \cap \Fix_G(y) \;\subseteq\; \Fix_G(z) \qquad \forall z \in [x, y],$$ where $[x, y]$ denotes the line segment joining $x$ and $y$ in $A$.

This is a convexity hypothesis on the fix groups along geodesic segments. It plays two essential roles:

  • it makes [[node:building.contraction_extension_K3|the contraction map extend $G$-equivariantly]] to $\BSigma_x$;
  • it is checked separately for classical groups ([[node:applications.classical_K1_K2_K3]]) and for tame types ([[node:applications.tame_hypotheses_K]]), so the rest of the theory applies uniformly.

(K3) should be thought of as the geometric counterpart of the standard fact in Bruhat–Tits theory that $G_{x,r} \cap G_{y,r}$ embeds into $G_{z,r}$ for $z$ on $[x, y]$ — extended from Moy–Prasad subgroups to the full $\Fix_G$ groups along all of $G$.
